en: Oh my, that long ago?
Yeah. But I got the axe almost right away. Hehe.
Oh my goodness.
That's totally normal. Nagoya's a big city. Lots of folks must come from all over the place.
No, not at all. People rarely come to Nagoya from elsewhere, and not many of us leave to go anyplace else.
I see. Then outsiders must be rare.
See what I mean?
Nagoya can be a tough place for outsiders. Have you had a tough time here?
Yeah, I definitely experienced that first-hand. But maybe it's because the people here have a real strong sense of hometown pride.
Not at all. People downtown are all really nice to me. I'm greatly obliged to them.
I suppose they would be. But you've been in Nagoya for fifteen years, you said? That practically makes you a local, Shinada-san!
Haha, that's good to hear!
There are many families who have lived here for generations, so I suppose it's natural we would seem insular.
Makes sense. Come to think of it, there are tons of rich people here too! It's a different world than the one a broke guy like me lives in.
That's only a small number of us. Not everyone in Nagoya is wealthy.
Really? My image of Nagoya is one of glittering gold and in-your-face, gorgeous, rich people.
I think you're talking about those gold rooftop shachihoko ornaments. The people, not so much!
Seeing the lady before me, I beg to differ.
It doesn't bother me. I went through a lot, but this town has finally accepted me. I'm good.
I'm happy to hear you say that! This city can be so unfriendly toward outsiders.
I'm not sure I'd go that far.
Including your family?
My family is... not one of those, no.
Then do you know any of those families? I don't hear other people describe things as insular much.
This... This is a rather private matter. Do you mind not asking me about it?
Oh, sorry about that. I was caught up in the conversation, that's all.
Really? How come people don't leave Nagoya all that much? Nobody ever moves away to Tokyo or Osaka?
No, everyone works for local businesses, so there's really no need to move elsewhere.
Wow. That must make class reunions way easier, at least.
Ahaha! I hadn't thought of that! I suppose you have a point.
I haven't kept in touch with my old classmates at all, though. They've probably forgotten about me.
Did you just... sigh? That's not like you. Is something the matter?
My mother found out that I work here.
Busted, huh? I hear that happens a lot. Lots of girls try to hide where they work, but most of them get found out eventually.
Yes. My mother wasn't upset with me, but I still feel like I've done something to be ashamed of.
So what? Being a hostess isn't unusual in this day and age. It's not the sort of thing you need to hide from your parents anymore.
No, and I'm not overly concerned by it, either. But I feel guilty about having kept it a secret for so long.
None of my other girlfriends are working, so I'd be somewhat ashamed if our neighbors found out.
None of them? What do they all do?
Housework and the like. The ones who are married are dedicated housewives, I imagine.
Being rich sounds awesome! I wish I could live a life like that.
Perhaps you should find yourself a benefactor, Shinada-san.
Sure! I'd love the chance to freeload at some rich household.
Well, a good many artists and musicians are invited to take up residence at wealthy estates.
I'm... not exactly talented in those ways. My only redeeming quality is my hard-cut bod.
Oh, but there are individuals who support athletes financially as well.
Whoa, there are?
Maybe not. I think I'd feel like a moocher. I'd rather make an honest living, even if it means being poor.
That's just something normal people tell themselves in order to feel better. Wouldn't it be better to live in wealth and comfort?
See, that's a tough call. I don't really think it's that simple.
Do you think I should quit my job in consideration of what our neighbors may think?
Yes. If it's going to be even somewhat problematic, you're better off quitting.
You think so too, Shinada-san? All right. I'll discuss things with my mother.
You can't! If you did that, I'd never get to see you again, Shion-chan.
Hehe. Oh, you tell such pretty lies, Shinada-san. Thank you for the sentiment!
It's not a lie. I'm super into you!
What do you do at home? I guess when you're not at work, it's all free time?
Oh, no. I have all sorts of lessons to take. They're harder than you might expect.
That's work? Can't be.
A proper woman must undergo domestic training. Otherwise, I'd never find a husband.
But how the heck are you ever supposed to meet a guy? Why not get out there and find somebody?
Oh, mine is sure to be an arranged marriage. It would be improper for me to seek out a partner on my own.
Oh. Are you sure you'll be happy with that?
How'd your secret get out, anyway?
Ah. It's something of an embarrassing story.
When I started work, they told me I needed to be financially independent from my parents for tax purposes. I avoided it for some time, but I finally told my mother.
She asked me if I was working part-time somewhere, and I wound up telling her everything.
You shot yourself in the foot. If you'd kept quiet, she'd never have known.
I had to tell her to complete the process. Otherwise, it would have been tax evasion.
Hmm. I guess if you needed the money, it couldn't be helped. Living at home can be really rough.
Why not lie? You didn't have to tell her you were working anywhere.
But wouldn't it be odd if I were making money without having a job?
So think of a better lie. Even people in debt make up all sorts of lies to delay payments.
You need to be able to pull that sort of thing off to become a proper adult, Shion-chan.
Oh dear! I know it's wrong to deceive one's parents, but the thought alone is thrilling! How would I get money without working, indeed? The possibilities are intriguing.
Heh. Just don't do it too much, or they'll never believe you again.
Shinada-san? I'd like your advice on something.
Ask away, m'lady!
It's... Well, it's something quite inappropriate for me to ask you about.
What sort of thing?
Don't worry. You can talk to me about anything.
Oh, thank you so much! I knew you'd say that, Shinada-san!
Really? Hey cool, I'm glad you trust me.
Employees from a big-name company in Nagoya are regulars at our club, and they had their year-end party the other day.
The manager said we'd get a bonus if we went as companions to this event, and so a number of our girls did just that.
Did you go too?
Yes. It was a good chance to hand out my card.
Haha, that's pretty clever!
I didn't know hostesses did that sort of thing. I've heard of buying out a club for a night, but sending girls off-site must make a lot of money.
I'd never done it before, but our clients said they had money to burn. The club apparently made quite a profit.
Hey, if there's money burning, send some my way instead!
So I met one of the directors at the company, and he was quite smitten with me.
Hehe, way to go, Shion-chan! You know how to work people who have money, huh?
Well, after we met outside the club a few times, he wound up proposing to me.
Hot damn! That's a little fast, isn't it?
Quite. I had no idea he'd been thinking of me like that, so it came as quite a shock!
What are you going to do? You didn't say yes to him, did you?
Yet!? You mean you didn't turn him down on the spot?
Hehe. You're quite perceptive, Shinada-san. But yes, this is why I'm somewhat troubled.
You're going to turn him down though, right?
...Are you thinking of saying yes?
I'm still thinking it over. Maybe it would be best if I accepted.
You have to turn him down. There's no way this will turn out well.
How can you really be sure of that if you don't even know the gentleman?
Oh, I know him alright. This guy is into hostesses. If he gets married, that's not going to stop. I guarantee you he's gonna be a cheater.
Goodness, why would you jump to such a cynical conclusion? I thought you were better than that.
There's nothing to suggest he'd make a poor husband, so I have no reason to tell him no.
Isn't not loving him reason enough?
In my world, arranged marriages are the norm. Few of us ever marry out of love.
Have you talked to your family?
Why not? This is a big deal. It's got to be too much to handle all on your own.
If I tell my mother, she's certain to be in favor of the idea, and I can't go against anything she tells me to do.
So, you're trying to decide for yourself. I guess there's not much I can tell you then.
You're right. All I've done is trouble you. I'm sorry for even bringing up this conversation.
Don't be silly! I'll always be here to support you, Shion-chan.
Do you remember the client I talked to you about the other day?
What about him?
Who again? Sorry, I don't remember who you mean.
You know, the businessman from that company that invited me to their year end party.
Oh, that guy! What about him?
I told my mother about his marriage proposal.
Yes. At first she was pleased, but as I told her more about him, her disapproval grew.
How come? Isn't this guy a big-shot at some huge corporation? I figured she'd be bouncing off her gilded rocker.
She's actually worried because his family's social standing is too high for us.
Oh wow! Ha, I didn't realize you rich folks had to consider that sort of thing for marriage.
It's not just the marriage itself to consider. There will be problems down the line if the two families have to maintain a relationship.
Things would get pretty tense, I bet.
Sounds complicated. This is why I'm not down with getting married. Or being rich. Ha, just kidding, I'd still want to be rich.
Oh, Shinada-san! I thought that the reason you hadn't gotten married was because you haven't found a fiancée!
Hey, that's got nothing to do with it!
Wait, are you seriously going to turn him down because of what your mother thinks?
Because if my mother gives her blessing, I'll get married. And if she says no, then I can't.
Ah, I see. But you need to turn him down pronto. You can't leave the guy hanging like this.
I can't. I have yet to receive a direction from my mother.
Okay, I get it. Then sounds like this conversation is over.
It doesn't matter what I say. All you care about is what your mother thinks, so anything I suggest is about as useful as milkin' a monkey.
I'm sorry, Shinada-san. This was quite improper of me.
Apology accepted. Sometimes just having an ear to listen to your problems makes things seem not so bad. I'm always here if you need to talk to someone.
You really have been a big help, Shinada-san.
Hey, of course you're going to freak out about getting married. It's not a simple subject.
You don't have to apologize. I just want to know what it is you want to do, not your mother.
Stand up for yourself! Who's getting married here, anyway? You, or your mother?
Well, I am, of course, but...
Then who cares about your family? Do what you want to do, and screw the rest.
I can't do that. There's no point for me to get married if my mother isn't happy for me.
I just don't get it. All I gotta say is, don't choose a path you're gonna end up regretting later. You'll, well, regret it.
Because all I'm hearing about is what your mother wants. Sounds to me like an excuse to put off making a decision.
You really are insightful, Shinada-san. It's a little disconcerting how well you know me.
Heh, I've just got a knack for reading people. But if you really don't know, you should probably think about it a little harder.
That's really weird. Why do your parents pick who you get married to?
Arranged marriage is the norm here in Nagoya. In fact, it's somewhat strange that I'm the one telling my mother about the proposal.
That's not normal at all. Sounds more like a feudal samurai clan than a family.
Hm, perhaps so. I suppose women back in those times would have had thoughts similar to mine, no?
Uh, yeah, definitely weird.
Lately, I've been getting the feeling that somebody's following me.
Wait, what!? Who?
Seriously? What the heck makes you think that?
Yeah, me! I've always got my eye on you, my darling Shion-chan!
Could you please not joke about this? I know it isn't you, Shinada-san.
Sorry, sorry.
Like I was saying, whenever I leave my house or the club, it feels like someone is watching me.
